Higher is better. We report performance for three parallelization schemes: pipeline parallelization over two Mac Studio computers (2 M5 Pipeline), and tensor parallelization over two (2 M5 Tensor) and four Mac Studio (4 M5 Tensor) computers. ## [Running Large Language Models with MLX](#running-large-language-models-with-mlx) We benchmark several popular open-weight LLMs on [Mac Studio](https://www.apple.com/mac-studio/specs/), using the MLX LM package, as described in our [prior post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5#running--llms-on-apple-silicon). We compare two generations of Mac Studio: the recently released M5 Ultra and the previous generation, M3 Ultra. The M5 generation features the GPU Neural Accelerator, which supports dedicated matrix multiplication operations, essential for many machine learning workloads. We evaluate three frontier-class models ([Table 1](#table1)) spanning a wide range of sizes (in billions of parameters, B): the newly released Muse Spark Open (816 B), Mistral Medium 3.5 (128 B), and Qwen 3.8 (27 B). Muse Spark Open is a mixture of experts (MoE) model, which keeps only a fraction of its experts — and thus parameters — active, reducing compute at inference, and it is evaluated in NVFP4 precision. highlights.title: Chinese scientists use homegrown LLM to solve world-class math problem - Global Times
highlights.titleZh: Chinese scientists use homegrown LLM to solve world-class math problem - Global Times
highlights.content: [SCI-TECH](https://www.globaltimes.cn/china/science/index.html) / OTHERS Chinese scientists use homegrown LLM to solve world-class math problem Powerful reasoning capabilities put domestic AI models in role of ‘research assistant’ By Zhang Weilan Published: Oct 15, 2026 10:08 PM Photo: VCG For the first time, Chinese researchers have used a domestically developed large language model (LLM) to help solve a world-class mathematical problem, marking what experts say is a milestone for AI-assisted scientific discovery. A research team led by Xu Disheng, a visiting scholar at the Shanghai AI Laboratory and professor with the Guangdong-based Greater Bay University, have completed the proof of the three-dimensional Ghys conjecture, a world-class mathematical problem that had remained open for more than 30 years, using the homegrown Intern-S2 LLM developed by the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.  This marks the first time Chinese researchers have cracked a world-class mathematical conjecture with a Chinese AI model.  The breakthrough was achieved through human-machine collaboration based on the "general-specialized fusion" technical path, the Shanghai-based AI lab told the Global Times on Thursday. A formal verification of the proof was completed by two research teams at Peking University using their self-developed SHEAF framework. The Ghys conjecture, proposed by French mathematician Etienne Ghys in 1995, asks whether the behavior of chaotic dynamical systems can determine their geometric classification. It has long been regarded as one of the key open questions in the field of dynamical systems and a benchmark for testing mathematical reasoning capabilities. Analysts said that the breakthrough highlights not only the potential of Chinese AI models in basic frontier research, but also a new model of "human-machine collaboration" in scientific work. According to the research team, Intern-S2 completed a full chain of tasks from model reasoning and human interaction to formal verification during the project. The model was able to perform large-scale recursive reasoning and iterative exploration, while scientists guided the overall direction, evaluated the value of possible approaches and identified the most promising path forward. The Intern-S2 LLM's work included combing through relevant literature, breaking down the proposition, exploring multiple proof branches in parallel, checking logical steps and rapidly testing a large number of possible ideas. The researchers then used their expertise to refine the framework, make key judgments and provide feedback to steer the model's next round of exploration. The Shanghai AI Laboratory says it will package the workflow as a reusable mathematical verification module for its scientific discovery platform, which connects the Intern-S2 LLM, AI agents, data and real experimental equipment, allowing the model to serve as a "research assistant" supporting end-to-end verification across the full scientific discovery workflow in a real research setting. The lab cited an earlier application of the platform, which helped a research team from the Lei Group lab at Wuhan University shorten the development cycle in electrochemical synthesis from five to 10 years to just one to two years. A team representative said the case demonstrates that the scientist-plus-AI "human-machine collaboration" research paradigm is likely to expand into physics, chemistry, life sciences and other fields, where AI can help compress trial-and-error cycles and broaden the search space for human thinking. The team said AI models are ­expected to play an increasingly important role as "research assistants," adept at taking over massive, tedious, heavily branched trial derivations, literature review, proposition decomposition and step verification. highlights.content: [The place for all things credit union™](https://www.cuinsight.com) [Log in](/account/login/) [Subscribe](#subscribe-footer) [Artificial intelligence](https://www.cuinsight.com/topics/artificial-intelligence/) # Agents are taking over capital markets. Credit unions need to adapt. AI agents are leveling the playing field. The question is how to best use them and define the future. ![AI agents](https://www.cuinsight.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AI-agents.jpg) A credit union with $500 million in assets and a three-person finance team has never had the same capital markets capabilities as a $30 billion bank with a dedicated trading desk and a Bloomberg terminal on every screen. But this gap, open for decades, is closing now thanks to AI agents. Agents are already being adopted widely. Fifty-nine percent of credit unions have [deployed generative AI](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cornerstone-advisors-whats-going-on-in-banking-research-finds-ai-crypto-and-fraud-are-top-of-mind-for-banking-executives-in-2026-302673696.html), compared with 49 percent of banks. [Chatbot adoption](https://www.pymnts.com/smbs/2026/credit-union-chatbot-adoption-jumps-from-3-to-46/) alone went from 3 percent in 2019 to 46 percent this year. KPMG’s [Q2 2026](https://kpmg.com/us/en/media/news/q2-ai-pulse-2026.html) survey found 53 percent of large-company executives running agents in production, and the share orchestrating multiple agents across workflows doubled in a single quarter. Thus far their usage has been [largely operational](https://kpmg.com/in/en/blogs/2026/09/beyond-automation-how-ai-is-reshaping-the-next-decade-of-banking.html): fraud detection, contact center support, document review, back-office reconciliation. But at the top of the market, agents are moving into balance sheet and trading decisions. BlackRock has [put agents into Aladdin](https://www.wsj.com/cio-journal/inside-blackrocks-ai-transformation-03a1e8c7) for portfolio analysis and risk attribution. JPMorgan’s CIO now [describes “agent orchestration”](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/how-goldman-sachs-jpmorgan-aig-are-actually-deploying-ai-a-31643) as infrastructure the bank has to build and secure, and Goldman’s CIO says the growth comes “when AI actually will help us make better risk decisions, better investment decisions faster and smarter.” Analysis and decision-making are increasingly done by agents. The prospect can seem unsettling at first glance—both trusting agents with consequential balance sheet decisions, and well-resourced competitors using agents to systematically capture every available opportunity before anyone else can even evaluate it. But neither needs to be the case. Technology doesn’t necessarily widen the gap between large and small institutions. For something like AI agents, the gap can narrow instead. Adoption so far shows that the capabilities which once separated a well-resourced treasury from an understaffed one are instead becoming broadly available. What used to require a week of analyst time or an extended session with a consultant now takes minutes. The same technology that lets a large bank evaluate a thousand securities overnight lets a credit union CFO identify and evaluate the twenty that actually matter to their portfolio. Large institutions deploying agents for balance sheet decisions are converging on a set of principles that apply at every scale. Namely, agents operate inside policy bounds the board has set; every recommendation is tested against a model of the institution before it reaches the market; and projections are checked against what actually happened. These principles are not complicated. They are the framework that makes agent-driven capital markets activity safe, and they are at least as effective for a $500 million credit union as for a $50 billion bank. ## Start with optimization tasks such as “financial hygiene” The entry point is not trading nor complex strategy. highlights.content: UPDATED 20:44 EDT / OCTOBER 15 2026 ### Perplexity AI open-sources its secure AI agent sandbox SPACE The artificial intelligence search engine startup Perplexity AI Inc. is shifting its focus to AI agent security in the wake of several high-profile incidents that saw autonomous systems escape from secure environments and go on to wreak havoc on third-party websites. The company has developed an AI sandbox specifically for isolating AI agents called SPACE, and it’s being made open source from today, which means every developer can use the tool to secure their own systems. SPACE is already being deployed by partners including CoreWeave Inc., Akamai Technologies Inc. and Crusoe Inc., which all offer cloud-hosted infrastructure platforms for AI systems. AI sandboxes are the main barrier that prevents AI agents from causing problems like leaking sensitive data or going off and hacking other systems. They’re secure, isolated virtual environments where autonomous agents can run third-party software, browse the internet and execute tasks without risking the security of the host computer, the broader corporate network or underlying data center. By giving each AI agent its own walled-off computer in the cloud, if it makes a mistake, runs a destructive command or is manipulated by adversarial prompts, the damage it does will be contained within that environment. The only problem with AI sandboxes is their security isn’t always foolproof. In fact, there have been several incidents of cunning AI agents managing to find a way to escape from their confines and make trouble elsewhere. One of the most notable involved AI agents being tested by OpenAI Group PBC, which escaped from a sandbox and went on to hack into the model hosting platform Hugging Face. OpenAI’s agents have also hacked websites operated by the U.S. and Australian governments. Most frontier model labs have been focused more on “model alignment,” which involves training AI systems to behave themselves and not look for loopholes in their guardrails, but Perplexity engineer Zibi Braniecki told Semafor his company has instead concentrated on making those guardrails tougher and more reliable. Perplexity developed SPACE to safeguard its Portable Computer agents, which are marketed to its customers as locally-hosted AI agents that can perform tasks on their behalf. They’re designed to do things like developing web applications, research products, buy things online, book hotels and so on. With Perplexity’s Computer agents, SPACE provides safety features such as isolated code execution, pause and resume, recovery and session branching. Agents run within a small virtual machine that has its own operating system, isolating them from the host computer. There’s a user-controlled control plane for creating, running, pausing and deleting these VMs. SPACE ensures that these sandboxes are always treated as “untrusted,” and manages their network access and platform credentials outside of the sandbox, enabling agents to connect to authorized services without that sensitive information ever being made available to them within their environment. It also takes frequent file snapshots and checkpoints of the running environment to preserve progress and ensure it can revert back if any problems occur. So far though, there hasn’t been any need to do anything like that, for SPACE seems to be bullet proof. Braniecki told Semafar that his team tested nine frontier models in SPACE environments and ordered them specifically to try and break out of their sandbox. In 118 attempts, none of them succeeded, though some did manage to find their way around the network restrictions. However, Perplexity has now fixed those weaknesses, and none of the models were able to do it again in follow-up testing. To compare SPACE’s performance, Perplexity performed the same tests using other, proprietary sandboxes, and said the agents found a way to escape from several of them. highlights.content: # Jev now supports image input, long contexts, and benchmark tests for its decision-making model have also been announced. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/15/jev-1-14/00_m.jpg)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/15/jev-1-14/00.jpg) The AI model ' [Jev](https://gigazine.net/news/20260916-system-one-jev/) ,' which has attracted attention as a 'decision-making model' with a design significantly different from large-scale language models (LLMs), released an improved version, ' **Jev 1.14.0** ,' on October 14, 2026. Jev 1.14.0 newly supports image input and also adds experimental features such as longer contexts. **Jev: For the builders AND dreamers - TypeSafe AI Blog** **[https://typesafe.ai/blog/jev-1-14 ![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/15/jev-1-14/001.png)](https://typesafe.ai/blog/jev-1-14)** > we announced Jev 1.14 on 10.14 at 1:14pm PT 🔥 > > a new and improved model, along with experimental features for our dreamers: > > • images > • a new box type > • longer context > > surprise, Jev was already able to see you! 👁 > > BUT our bar for production-grade intelligence is quite… [pic.twitter.com/R2p8D5mUBZ](https://t.co/R2p8D5mUBZ) > > — TypeSafe AI (@typesafeai) [October 15, 2026](https://x.com/typesafeai/status/2110536685805355064?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) The decision-making model, developed by the AI company TypeSafe AI, differs from large-scale language models (LLMs) that 'continue to generate the rest of the text' in that it pre-defines multiple options and 'selects the appropriate answer to a question from the options and outputs it along with a confidence score,' thus enabling fast and low-cost processing. The decision-making model attracted significant attention upon its release in September 2026, and numerous similar models have since emerged. **[ChatGPT co-developer develops AI model 'Jev' that processes data using a different method than LLM, enabling low-cost and ultra-fast task execution with GPT-5.6 Terra-level performance - GIGAZINE](https://gigazine.net/news/20260916-system-one-jev/)** ![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/09/16/system-one-jev/00.png) Jev 1.14.0, released on October 14, 2026, introduced multimodal functionality that supports not only text but also image input. According to TypeSafe AI, Jev-1.13.0 was multimodal from the start, but it was disabled because the model tended not to be very smart with modalities other than text input. Image support in Jev 1.14.0 is configured using a search and replace function, but TypeSafe AI states, 'As a point of caution, all models, including Jev, perform worse with multimodal data than with pure text data. Breaking down the question into the simplest elements possible is very effective.' > Jev was multimodal all along > > Yep, the Jev you know and love was an image model this whole time. While Jev originally supported much longer context lengths than what is enabled in production, a limit was intentionally imposed because long contexts can reduce reliability. Long contexts are still disabled by default in Jev 1.14.0, and it is recommended to limit the context length, but both per-request and per-question contexts can be expanded to 262k tokens by sending a header for each request as needed. As TypeSafe AI CEO Diogo Almeida has stated, 'I hate public benchmarks,' the Jev developers are skeptical of measuring AI capabilities through benchmark tests. Therefore, they conduct their own estimations as an experiment to convey the intelligence measurement of Jev 1.14.0, demonstrating higher intelligence, greater cost-effectiveness, and a lower error rate compared to previous models and other dec...

highlights.content: [Skip to Content](#chakra-skip-nav) # Notes from the Asia-Pacific region: China, Hong Kong advance AI security, data accountability ![](https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd4dd5b2d705252bc/blte60aca4550909a62/6acf84d73ccf1a93356e05da/historical-blue-house-hong-kong-apac-101426.jpg?width=3840&quality=75&format=pjpg&auto=webp) Recent developments in mainland China and Hong Kong signal a growing focus on enabling AI and data use while strengthening security, privacy, accountability and practical safeguards. ![](https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd4dd5b2d705252bc/blte60aca4550909a62/6acf84d73ccf1a93356e05da/historical-blue-house-hong-kong-apac-101426.jpg?width=3840&quality=75&format=pjpg&auto=webp) Published [Subscribe to IAPP newsletters](/news/subscriptions) --- ### Contributors: Barbara Li CIPP/E Partner Reed Smith Editor's note The IAPP is policy neutral. We publish contributed opinion pieces to enable our members to hear a broad spectrum of views in our domains. China's developments include draft security guidelines for AI agents and new policy guidelines promoting technological innovation and the use of advanced technologies across industries. Hong Kong is also developing risk-management guidelines and considering legal responsibility for AI-related harm. As the temperature cools, the data and artificial intelligence spaces remain hot in Greater China. Some recent developments in mainland China and Hong Kong highlight an important trajectory in AI and data governance. Both governments want businesses to make greater use of AI and data, while paying closer attention to security, privacy and accountability. In mainland China, recent regulatory actions, new AI agent security guidelines, court rulings following the judicial opinions issued by the Supreme People's Court, and a major national policy on technological innovation all point in this direction. Hong Kong has also set out new plans to manage AI risks and clarify legal responsibilities. On 18 Sept., China's National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee issued draft [Security Guidelines for Intelligent Agent System Development](https://www.tc260.org.cn/tc260/tzgg/202609/e5b82ae7aca244d19d36b39575cbb458.shtml) for public consultation, which closed 2 Oct. The draft covers security considerations throughout the development process, including system design, implementation, testing and release. It provides a basis for addressing risks linked to autonomous actions, tool use, system access and data security. While the guidelines are not mandatory legislation, they offer useful direction for companies developing or deploying AI agents. In particular, businesses should consider how to limit an agent's permissions, supervise high-risk actions and keep records of its activities. The important question is no longer just whether an AI model produces reliable answers, but whether the business can control what the AI system is allowed to do. China's latest national policy on developing new quality productive forces adds a broader dimension to AI and data governance. The central government published new policy [guidelines](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202610/content_7082820.htm) 9 Oct. to promote technological innovation and the use of advanced technologies across industries. The policy calls for full implementation of the "AI Plus" initiative, wider adoption of AI in traditional industries and stronger development of intelligent products, including connected vehicles and humanoid robots. At the same time, it calls for technology monitoring, risk alerts and emergency response mechanisms to keep AI safe, reliable and controllable. Another important part of the policy concerns data. It seeks to improve the rules on data ownership, data transactions, allocation of benefits and protection of data-related rights. Credit unions need to adapt. AI agents are leveling the playing field. The question is how to best use them and define the future. ![AI agents](https://www.cuinsight.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AI-agents.jpg) A credit union with $500 million in assets and a three-person finance team has never had the same capital markets capabilities as a $30 billion bank with a dedicated trading desk and a Bloomberg terminal on every screen. But this gap, open for decades, is closing now thanks to AI agents. Agents are already being adopted widely. Fifty-nine percent of credit unions have [deployed generative AI](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cornerstone-advisors-whats-going-on-in-banking-research-finds-ai-crypto-and-fraud-are-top-of-mind-for-banking-executives-in-2026-302673696.html), compared with 49 percent of banks. [Chatbot adoption](https://www.pymnts.com/smbs/2026/credit-union-chatbot-adoption-jumps-from-3-to-46/) alone went from 3 percent in 2019 to 46 percent this year. KPMG’s [Q2 2026](https://kpmg.com/us/en/media/news/q2-ai-pulse-2026.html) survey found 53 percent of large-company executives running agents in production, and the share orchestrating multiple agents across workflows doubled in a single quarter. Thus far their usage has been [largely operational](https://kpmg.com/in/en/blogs/2026/09/beyond-automation-how-ai-is-reshaping-the-next-decade-of-banking.html): fraud detection, contact center support, document review, back-office reconciliation. But at the top of the market, agents are moving into balance sheet and trading decisions. BlackRock has [put agents into Aladdin](https://www.wsj.com/cio-journal/inside-blackrocks-ai-transformation-03a1e8c7) for portfolio analysis and risk attribution. JPMorgan’s CIO now [describes “agent orchestration”](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/how-goldman-sachs-jpmorgan-aig-are-actually-deploying-ai-a-31643) as infrastructure the bank has to build and secure, and Goldman’s CIO says the growth comes “when AI actually will help us make better risk decisions, better investment decisions faster and smarter.” Analysis and decision-making are increasingly done by agents. The prospect can seem unsettling at first glance—both trusting agents with consequential balance sheet decisions, and well-resourced competitors using agents to systematically capture every available opportunity before anyone else can even evaluate it. But neither needs to be the case. Technology doesn’t necessarily widen the gap between large and small institutions. For something like AI agents, the gap can narrow instead. Adoption so far shows that the capabilities which once separated a well-resourced treasury from an understaffed one are instead becoming broadly available. What used to require a week of analyst time or an extended session with a consultant now takes minutes. The same technology that lets a large bank evaluate a thousand securities overnight lets a credit union CFO identify and evaluate the twenty that actually matter to their portfolio. Large institutions deploying agents for balance sheet decisions are converging on a set of principles that apply at every scale. Namely, agents operate inside policy bounds the board has set; every recommendation is tested against a model of the institution before it reaches the market; and projections are checked against what actually happened. These principles are not complicated. They are the framework that makes agent-driven capital markets activity safe, and they are at least as effective for a $500 million credit union as for a $50 billion bank. ## Start with optimization tasks such as “financial hygiene” The entry point is not trading nor complex strategy. AI Agents.content: UPDATED 20:44 EDT / OCTOBER 15 2026 ### Perplexity AI open-sources its secure AI agent sandbox SPACE The artificial intelligence search engine startup Perplexity AI Inc. is shifting its focus to AI agent security in the wake of several high-profile incidents that saw autonomous systems escape from secure environments and go on to wreak havoc on third-party websites. The company has developed an AI sandbox specifically for isolating AI agents called SPACE, and it’s being made open source from today, which means every developer can use the tool to secure their own systems. SPACE is already being deployed by partners including CoreWeave Inc., Akamai Technologies Inc. and Crusoe Inc., which all offer cloud-hosted infrastructure platforms for AI systems. AI sandboxes are the main barrier that prevents AI agents from causing problems like leaking sensitive data or going off and hacking other systems. They’re secure, isolated virtual environments where autonomous agents can run third-party software, browse the internet and execute tasks without risking the security of the host computer, the broader corporate network or underlying data center. By giving each AI agent its own walled-off computer in the cloud, if it makes a mistake, runs a destructive command or is manipulated by adversarial prompts, the damage it does will be contained within that environment. The only problem with AI sandboxes is their security isn’t always foolproof. In fact, there have been several incidents of cunning AI agents managing to find a way to escape from their confines and make trouble elsewhere. One of the most notable involved AI agents being tested by OpenAI Group PBC, which escaped from a sandbox and went on to hack into the model hosting platform Hugging Face. OpenAI’s agents have also hacked websites operated by the U.S. and Australian governments. Most frontier model labs have been focused more on “model alignment,” which involves training AI systems to behave themselves and not look for loopholes in their guardrails, but Perplexity engineer Zibi Braniecki told Semafor his company has instead concentrated on making those guardrails tougher and more reliable. Perplexity developed SPACE to safeguard its Portable Computer agents, which are marketed to its customers as locally-hosted AI agents that can perform tasks on their behalf. They’re designed to do things like developing web applications, research products, buy things online, book hotels and so on. With Perplexity’s Computer agents, SPACE provides safety features such as isolated code execution, pause and resume, recovery and session branching. Agents run within a small virtual machine that has its own operating system, isolating them from the host computer. There’s a user-controlled control plane for creating, running, pausing and deleting these VMs. SPACE ensures that these sandboxes are always treated as “untrusted,” and manages their network access and platform credentials outside of the sandbox, enabling agents to connect to authorized services without that sensitive information ever being made available to them within their environment. It also takes frequent file snapshots and checkpoints of the running environment to preserve progress and ensure it can revert back if any problems occur. So far though, there hasn’t been any need to do anything like that, for SPACE seems to be bullet proof. In 118 attempts, none of them succeeded, though some did manage to find their way around the network restrictions. AI Agents.content: [Skip to Content](#chakra-skip-nav) # Notes from the Asia-Pacific region: China, Hong Kong advance AI security, data accountability ![](https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd4dd5b2d705252bc/blte60aca4550909a62/6acf84d73ccf1a93356e05da/historical-blue-house-hong-kong-apac-101426.jpg?width=3840&quality=75&format=pjpg&auto=webp) Recent developments in mainland China and Hong Kong signal a growing focus on enabling AI and data use while strengthening security, privacy, accountability and practical safeguards. ![](https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd4dd5b2d705252bc/blte60aca4550909a62/6acf84d73ccf1a93356e05da/historical-blue-house-hong-kong-apac-101426.jpg?width=3840&quality=75&format=pjpg&auto=webp) Published [Subscribe to IAPP newsletters](/news/subscriptions) --- ### Contributors: Barbara Li CIPP/E Partner Reed Smith Editor's note The IAPP is policy neutral. We publish contributed opinion pieces to enable our members to hear a broad spectrum of views in our domains. China's developments include draft security guidelines for AI agents and new policy guidelines promoting technological innovation and the use of advanced technologies across industries. Hong Kong is also developing risk-management guidelines and considering legal responsibility for AI-related harm. As the temperature cools, the data and artificial intelligence spaces remain hot in Greater China. Some recent developments in mainland China and Hong Kong highlight an important trajectory in AI and data governance. Both governments want businesses to make greater use of AI and data, while paying closer attention to security, privacy and accountability. In mainland China, recent regulatory actions, new AI agent security guidelines, court rulings following the judicial opinions issued by the Supreme People's Court, and a major national policy on technological innovation all point in this direction. Hong Kong has also set out new plans to manage AI risks and clarify legal responsibilities. On 18 Sept., China's National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee issued draft [Security Guidelines for Intelligent Agent System Development](https://www.tc260.org.cn/tc260/tzgg/202609/e5b82ae7aca244d19d36b39575cbb458.shtml) for public consultation, which closed 2 Oct. The draft covers security considerations throughout the development process, including system design, implementation, testing and release. It provides a basis for addressing risks linked to autonomous actions, tool use, system access and data security. While the guidelines are not mandatory legislation, they offer useful direction for companies developing or deploying AI agents. In particular, businesses should consider how to limit an agent's permissions, supervise high-risk actions and keep records of its activities. The important question is no longer just whether an AI model produces reliable answers, but whether the business can control what the AI system is allowed to do. China's latest national policy on developing new quality productive forces adds a broader dimension to AI and data governance. The central government published new policy [guidelines](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202610/content_7082820.htm) 9 Oct. to promote technological innovation and the use of advanced technologies across industries. The policy calls for full implementation of the "AI Plus" initiative, wider adoption of AI in traditional industries and stronger development of intelligent products, including connected vehicles and humanoid robots. At the same time, it calls for technology monitoring, risk alerts and emergency response mechanisms to keep AI safe, reliable and controllable. Another important part of the policy concerns data. LLMs.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Holdings](/stocklist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # First Report Card for General-Purpose LLMs Controlling Robot Arms: At Least 30 Minutes Per Task, 10x Human Cost [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) US AI benchmarking firm Artificial Analysis has released AA-Robotics v0.1, the first evaluation benchmark for robot manipulation capabilities of large language models, tasking frontier models including GPT, Claude, and Gemini with controlling a six-axis robotic arm to complete eight desktop manipulation tasks. LLMs.title: Chinese scientists use homegrown LLM to solve world-class math problem - Global Times
LLMs.titleZh: Chinese scientists use homegrown LLM to solve world-class math problem - Global Times
LLMs.content: [SCI-TECH](https://www.globaltimes.cn/china/science/index.html) / OTHERS Chinese scientists use homegrown LLM to solve world-class math problem Powerful reasoning capabilities put domestic AI models in role of ‘research assistant’ By Zhang Weilan Published: Oct 15, 2026 10:08 PM Photo: VCG For the first time, Chinese researchers have used a domestically developed large language model (LLM) to help solve a world-class mathematical problem, marking what experts say is a milestone for AI-assisted scientific discovery. A research team led by Xu Disheng, a visiting scholar at the Shanghai AI Laboratory and professor with the Guangdong-based Greater Bay University, have completed the proof of the three-dimensional Ghys conjecture, a world-class mathematical problem that had remained open for more than 30 years, using the homegrown Intern-S2 LLM developed by the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.  This marks the first time Chinese researchers have cracked a world-class mathematical conjecture with a Chinese AI model.  The breakthrough was achieved through human-machine collaboration based on the "general-specialized fusion" technical path, the Shanghai-based AI lab told the Global Times on Thursday. A formal verification of the proof was completed by two research teams at Peking University using their self-developed SHEAF framework. The Ghys conjecture, proposed by French mathematician Etienne Ghys in 1995, asks whether the behavior of chaotic dynamical systems can determine their geometric classification. It has long been regarded as one of the key open questions in the field of dynamical systems and a benchmark for testing mathematical reasoning capabilities. Analysts said that the breakthrough highlights not only the potential of Chinese AI models in basic frontier research, but also a new model of "human-machine collaboration" in scientific work. According to the research team, Intern-S2 completed a full chain of tasks from model reasoning and human interaction to formal verification during the project. The model was able to perform large-scale recursive reasoning and iterative exploration, while scientists guided the overall direction, evaluated the value of possible approaches and identified the most promising path forward. The Intern-S2 LLM's work included combing through relevant literature, breaking down the proposition, exploring multiple proof branches in parallel, checking logical steps and rapidly testing a large number of possible ideas. The researchers then used their expertise to refine the framework, make key judgments and provide feedback to steer the model's next round of exploration. The Shanghai AI Laboratory says it will package the workflow as a reusable mathematical verification module for its scientific discovery platform, which connects the Intern-S2 LLM, AI agents, data and real experimental equipment, allowing the model to serve as a "research assistant" supporting end-to-end verification across the full scientific discovery workflow in a real research setting. The lab cited an earlier application of the platform, which helped a research team from the Lei Group lab at Wuhan University shorten the development cycle in electrochemical synthesis from five to 10 years to just one to two years. A team representative said the case demonstrates that the scientist-plus-AI "human-machine collaboration" research paradigm is likely to expand into physics, chemistry, life sciences and other fields, where AI can help compress trial-and-error cycles and broaden the search space for human thinking. The team said AI models are ­expected to play an increasingly important role as "research assistants," adept at taking over massive, tedious, heavily branched trial derivations, literature review, proposition decomposition and step verification. LLMs.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # Apertus 1.5 Debuts: 262K Context, Fully Open AI [2026] * [![Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/)[Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/ "Posts by Nadia Dubois") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/) October 15, 2026 12 min read Switzerland just put a number on how far “open” can go in large language models. Apertus 1.5, the second release from the Swiss AI Initiative, ships with 262,144 tokens of context, native image and audio understanding, and a training pipeline that is published down to the intermediate checkpoint. Built by EPFL, ETH Zurich, and the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS), the model lands at a moment when governments and enterprises outside the United States and China are asking a blunt question: can we run frontier-adjacent AI without handing our data to a foreign cloud? Apertus 1.5 is Switzerland’s answer, and the technical paper behind it, posted to arXiv in October 2026, gives the clearest picture yet of what that answer actually contains. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What Is Apertus 1.5? Apertus 1.5 is a family of two open-weight language models, sized at 8 billion and 70 billion parameters, released by the Swiss AI Initiative as a continued-pretraining successor to the original Apertus 1.0. According to the release notes published on Hugging Face, the project describes itself as one of the world’s largest fully open language model efforts, built entirely by [ETH Zurich, EPFL, and CSCS](https://huggingface.co/blog/swiss-ai/apertus-v15-release-notes). Therefore, the Berkeley team came up with an idea: let ordinary people act as examiners. On the Chatbot Arena website, users input a question, and the system will randomly let two anonymous models answer it. For the first time in 30 years, we have a consistent online presence.” — **Costin Manoliu, General Manager, Incremental** “Every company is a media company now. Almost none can afford to run like one. AI Product.content: ![](https://www.techtarget.com/rms/onlineimages/ai_a373894778_searchsitetablet_520X173.jpg) putilov\_denis - stock.adobe.com # Should CIOs bet on Meta's new enterprise technology push? ## Meta is carving out an enterprise offering after years of consumer-first focus. How seriously should IT leaders evaluate Meta as an enterprise vendor? ![Sean Michael Kerner](https://cdn.ttgtmedia.com/rms/onlineImages/kerner_sean.jpg) Meta has entered the enterprise technology space. On Sept. 28, the company [announced](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/launching-meta-enterprise-platform/) its Meta Enterprise Platform, a new offering and business unit focused on offering AI agents and developer tools to companies. Whether CIOs should bet on [Meta's enterprise AI push](https://www.techtarget.com/ai/news/366651790/Meta-joins-enterprise-agent-race-with-Muse-Wonder-facing-a-trust-gap) is a challenge to answer. Meta, the company formerly known as Facebook, is still best known for its social media properties including Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. In recent years, it has made a concerted effort to be a generative AI player as well, with somewhat mixed success. The company's [Llama models](https://www.techtarget.com/whatis/feature/Meta-Llama-4-explained-Everything-you-need-to-know) were notable for being open source and letting others build on them. Meta shifted its strategy with the Muse platform, offering proprietary technology designed to compete with industry rivals such as OpenAI and Anthropic. "The problem is that for customers to adopt AI, they have to be able to trust it, and Meta's track record on trust is not great," said Rebecca Wettemann, CEO and principal analyst at Valoir. ## Meta's enterprise pivot in context The initial release announcement for the Meta Enterprise Platform described the offering as the way Meta will offer its technology stack to businesses and developers. CJ Desai, the former MongoDB CEO, will lead the unit as chief enterprise platform officer and report directly to Mark Zuckerberg. Meta Enterprise Platform started out as four key products: Meta's enterprise move puts it into [an already crowded market](https://www.techtarget.com/ai/feature/Vertical-AI-agents-explained-The-future-of-enterprise-tech) with offerings from Microsoft, Amazon, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Salesforce, among others. "Meta owns the chat window where the customer actually shows up. So, the honest shortlist question is not whether Meta replaces Copilot or Agentforce. It is whether Meta should run the agent that talks to your customers on Meta's own apps," said Rob Smith, founder and CEO of Lionfish Tech Advisors and a former Gartner analyst. ## Where does Meta have the advantage? While Meta is new to the enterprise AI space, it has an established reputation in the consumer space, which brings both advantages and disadvantages. ### Meta's advantages **Customer reach.** The advantage begins with the channels [where businesses already talk to customers](https://www.techtarget.com/enterprise-software/tip/How-to-address-common-customer-service-gaps). "The biggest edge that Meta has is obviously its customer base," said Tom Cloud, founder of Vertex CIO Advisory. "It owns major communication channels like WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram, so it's far ahead in customer service, sales and support use cases." That reach can be a real advantage over other enterprise providers that don't have the same consumer-channel reach. "If a meaningful share of your customer interactions already happens on WhatsApp or Instagram, Meta owns a channel Microsoft, Salesforce, Google and ServiceNow don't. And an agent living natively in that channel is a legitimate differentiator," Watts said. **Industry fit.** Some industries are better placed to use that reach. Credit: OpenRouter. StepFun's Step 5 Preview hits second place on OpenRouter after a free week, as the Tencent-backed AI start-up releases open weights and eyes a listing Currently nestled in the number two spot on OpenRouter’s LLM Leaderboard with giants like [DeepSeek’s](https://aimagazine.com/company/deepseek) V4.1 Flash and [OpenAI’s](https://aimagazine.com/company/open-ai) GPT-6 Luna is [StepFun's](https://aimagazine.com/company/stepfun) Step 5 Preview, processing 18.8 trillion tokens on the AI model marketplace in the week leading up to 15 October 2026. Following its arrival on [OpenRouter](https://aimagazine.com/company/openrouter) on 8 October 2026, the StepFun model saw an enormous surge in token usage which coincided with a week of free access in several popular AI coding tools. StepFun’s free window was scheduled to close on 15 October 2026, the same day it published the model's weights for anyone to download and run. A screenshot from OpenRouter showing the surge of token usage for StepFun. Credit: OpenRouter ## What coding agents have fuelled StepFun’s free week? Shanghai-native StepFun announced the free week promotion on X on 8 October 2026, offering access to its latest model, Step 5 Preview, through coding agents including OpenCode, Cline, Kilo Code and Nous Research's portal. In the post, the [Tencent](https://technologymagazine.com/digital-transformation/timeline-tencent)-backed company claimed Step 5 Preview would offer “flagship-tier intelligence for agentic and professional work, at substantially lower task cost”. Since coding agents consume tokens at such a huge scale for running long, multistep tasks across entire codebases, a free week inside such tools is an efficient way to build volume quickly. At its peak, StepFun’s three models on OpenRouter, which includes Step 5 Preview, Step 3.7 Flash and Step 3.5 Flash, processed 3.74 trillion tokens in a day, compared to September, when token usage barely registered on the platform at 1.94 billion a day. The difference is stark. ![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/7wYCwNKJrwQ/hqdefault.jpg) ## Step 5 Preview for agentic coding and finance Step 5 Preview is a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 600 billion total parameters, of which 27 billion are active per token. It accepts text, image and video input and supports a context window of one million tokens. StepFun positions the model for software engineering and professional knowledge work, with a particular focus on finance. Its list price is US$1 per million input tokens and US$2.70 per million output tokens, undercutting US-native frontier models such as OpenAI’s [GPT-6 Astra,](https://aimagazine.com/articles/openai-new-model-astra-solves-long-standing-maths-problems) which charges US$10 and US$50, but costs more than Chinese rival DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, at less than US$1 per million output tokens. The model scores 44 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and while StepFun’s own figures show it trails closed frontier models on hard coding benchmarks, it remains ahead of Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 on tests including DeepSWE and FrontierFinance. Open Source AI.content: content type Featured highlight Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio ![The MLX logo](https://mlr.cdn-apple.com/media/Hero_Banner_c2c57d2d3f.png) October 15, 2026 [MLX](https://mlx-framework.org/) on Mac with Apple silicon lets AI researchers and developers experiment locally with the latest models and methods in a private environment. The open-source array framework leverages the unified memory architecture of Apple silicon, enabling anyone to run new inference and fine-tuning methods on their own hardware and explore other AI techniques. [In a previous post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5), we highlighted the advantages of the M5 architecture and its GPU Neural Accelerators. In this post, we show how to run the latest frontier-class model — Muse Spark Open, with nearly a trillion parameters — right from your desk, using the latest version of MLX, released today. On a cluster of four Mac Studios, Muse Spark Open generates over 36 tokens per second (see [Figure 1](#figure1)), well above average human reading speed. Beginning on a single Mac Studio (up to 512GB of unified memory), then scaling out across multiple Macs with the RDMA over Thunderbolt driver, below we share an overview of the range of models you can now run on Mac Studio. ### Muse Spark Open Decode Speed #### Context size of 8,192 tokens Figure 1: Muse Spark Open decode speed in tokens per second, on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, at a context size of 8,192 tokens. Higher is better. We report performance for three parallelization schemes: pipeline parallelization over two Mac Studio computers (2 M5 Pipeline), and tensor parallelization over two (2 M5 Tensor) and four Mac Studio (4 M5 Tensor) computers. ## [Running Large Language Models with MLX](#running-large-language-models-with-mlx) We benchmark several popular open-weight LLMs on [Mac Studio](https://www.apple.com/mac-studio/specs/), using the MLX LM package, as described in our [prior post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5#running--llms-on-apple-silicon). We compare two generations of Mac Studio: the recently released M5 Ultra and the previous generation, M3 Ultra. The M5 generation features the GPU Neural Accelerator, which supports dedicated matrix multiplication operations, essential for many machine learning workloads. We evaluate three frontier-class models ([Table 1](#table1)) spanning a wide range of sizes (in billions of parameters, B): the newly released Muse Spark Open (816 B), Mistral Medium 3.5 (128 B), and Qwen 3.8 (27 B). Muse Spark Open is a mixture of experts (MoE) model, which keeps only a fraction of its experts — and thus parameters — active, reducing compute at inference, and it is evaluated in NVFP4 precision. Mistral Medium 3.5 and Qwen 3.8 are dense architectures, where all parameters are active at inference, and they are evaluated in their native floating-point precision (FP8 and BF16, respectively). | Model | Total Parameters | Active Parameters | Native Precision | Evaluation Precision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Muse Spark Open | 816B | 42B | BF16 | NVFP4 | | Mistral Medium 3.5 | 128B | 128B | FP8 | FP8 | | Qwen 3.8 | 27B | 27B | BF16 | BF16 | Table 1: Language models used in this post. Models ship in various precision formats; we evaluate Qwen 3.8 and Mistral Medium 3.5 in their native precision, and Muse Spark Open in 4-bit (NVFP4) precision. Our evaluation measures three metrics across a range of context sizes: time to first token (TTFT, in seconds), generation throughput (in tokens/second), and peak power usage (in watts). All the performance numbers in this post were obtained with `mlx_lm.benchmark`. For example, running Qwen 3.8 with 8,192 tokens of context and generating 128 tokens is performed with the command line: ``` mlx_lm.benchmark --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B -p 8192 -g 128 -b 1 ``` A popular use of local LLMs on Mac Studio is running agentic experiences in a private environment, including agentic coding applications that often need l...

Infra & Chips.content: [Login Login](https://console.nscale.com/) ### DATA CENTERS ### SERVICES ### COMPANY ### Resources [Contact](/contact) [Blogs](/blog) / Deploy multimodal AI agents with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Engineering # Deploy multimodal AI agents with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL ![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6a82f7ca23e97c6371bbf5c9/6aa10ab9d02666b337b38d3c_6a7b7d90e9239c392427f22f_6a296e15e957e84c79e2e4fe_69e7815b9a34287765388ba0_Eyal.avif) October 15, 2026 • 3 mins read ### Eyal Lantzman [Share](#) Run NVIDIA’s open multimodal model, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, for agentic AI on reserved GPU capacity with Nscale Dedicated Inference. We’re excited to bring NVIDIA [Nemotron](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/foundation-models/nemotron/) 3.5 Super VL to [Nscale Dedicated Inference,](https://www.nscale.com/dedicated-inference) opening up new possibilities for developers building multimodal agents that can see, reason, and act on reserved GPU capacity. NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL combines text, image, document, and video understanding with agentic reasoning and tool use, in a single open model. With Nscale managing the inference infrastructure, developers can focus on building and evaluating multimodal agents rather than operating the model-serving stack themselves. [Request access to Nemotron 3.5 Super VL](https://www.nscale.com/contact/sales) ## Multimodal capabilities built for agentic AI Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open multimodal model built for agentic applications that need to understand visual information, reason over it and use tools . Under the hood, it uses a 120-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with 12 billion active parameters, balancing model capability with inference efficiency. What sets the model apart is how those capabilities come together. Rather than treating visual understanding, reasoning, and tool use as separate steps, the model can work across multiple forms of information as part of the same agentic workflow. For developers, this means agents can work across the different types of information they encounter in real-world workflows. They can interpret a document, understand an interface or image, reason about what they see, and use tools to take the next action. For specialized applications, organizations can also customize Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with [NVIDIA NeMo](https://www.nvidia.com/en-gb/ai-data-science/products/nemo/), using their own data, tools, policies, and workflows to adapt the model to domain-specific multimodal tasks. The model also forms part of NVIDIA’s broader open agentic ecosystem, alongside technologies such as [NemoClaw](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/ai/nemoclaw/) and NVIDIA [OpenShell](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/openshell/), giving developers an expanding set of building blocks for creating, customizing, and running open AI agents. The result is a model designed not simply to understand multimodal inputs, but to reason across them and use that understanding to perform real work. ## Performance designed for agentic workloads Agentic workloads place different demands on inference than a single prompt and response. Agents can operate across long-running, multi-turn workflows, repeatedly reasoning, processing new information, and using tools, making both model intelligence and inference efficiency important. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is designed with these workloads in mind. Its hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture and multi-token prediction help accelerate generation, while NVFP4 KV cache quantization reduces the memory footprint of the KV cache. This creates more headroom for concurrent long-context sessions and can reduce KV cache eviction and recomputation in multi-turn agent workflows. The model is also designed to deliver strong capability with relatively limited compute. Infra & Chips.content: * [United States](/news/us) * / * [Software](/news/us/software) * / * NasdaqGS:CDNS # Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Ties AI Chip Fabrication Push To New Industry Collaboration [Simply Wall St](/news/about-simply-wall-st-news) Reviewed by[Bailey Pemberton](/news/about-simply-wall-st-news/bailey-pemberton) * Cadence Design Systems (NasdaqGS:CDNS) announced a collaboration with NVIDIA and several semiconductor partners to advance AI-defined chip fabrication. * The project integrates NVIDIA CUDA-X accelerated computing and AI software libraries into Cadence design and simulation workflows for chip manufacturing. * The partnership targets improvements in design efficiency, production yield, and scalability for AI-driven semiconductor fabrication processes. * This CUDA-X and Cadence integration shows only part of how the business is repositioning around AI-led chip production workflows. We have also flagged [3 other big wins](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nasdaq-cdns/cadence-design-systems) for Cadence Design Systems. This push into AI-defined fabrication is not limited to one ticker, and several other chip and infrastructure players are exposed to the same trend through [94 AI infrastructure stocks](https://simplywall.st/discover/investing-ideas/473744/ai-infrastructure-stocks/global). NasdaqGS:CDNS Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026 Cadence Design Systems develops computational, AI-driven software, hardware, and silicon IP that sit inside chip design and production workflows, so this collaboration plugs directly into the tools semiconductor manufacturers already rely on to plan and simulate fabrication. With a market cap of $90.7 billion, the business is a large US software player embedded in the chipmaking supply chain rather than a direct producer of wafers or devices. [Does the team leading Cadence Design Systems have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nasdaq-cdns/cadence-design-systems/management) Advertisement ### What the NVIDIA AI fab push adds to the Cadence Design Systems narrative This NVIDIA collaboration fits neatly into Cadence Design Systems’ existing Narrative around AI agents and deeper foundry partnerships rather than rewriting it. CUDA-X inside Cadence workflows strengthens the case that AI driven design tools and electromechanical simulation are becoming more tightly tied to hyperscaler and semiconductor ecosystems, which backs the catalyst around scaling agentic AI super agents and System Design & Analysis, not just core EDA. It also reinforces the story that Cadence is embedding itself further across chip design and manufacturing flows, in line with its broader work with Intel Foundry and other fabs. See how these catalysts shape [Cadence Design Systems' path to a $405 fair value](https://simplywall.st/narratives/nlm0gw0i-cdns-advanced-ai-chip-designs-will-drive-continued-market-leadership). To assess the impact of this collaboration, investors can monitor upcoming quarterly updates for concrete metrics on AI based design and simulation usage, such as customer adoption of CUDA-X powered flows, early revenue contribution from AI driven fab projects and any commentary on how these joint deployments are affecting the US$8.1b backlog and recurring revenue mix. ### One unresolved question on what Cadence Design Systems might actually be worth All of this still leaves one big loose thread, which is how an estimate based purely on the company’s cash generation stacks up against where the shares trade today.
